content: Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, has the potential to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of drugs metabolized by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction may lead to an elevated risk of adverse reactions associated with these substrates. The following are specific considerations for co-administration with lenacapavir: 1. Fenofibric Acid: Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of fenofibric acid by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 2. Fentanyl (all formulations): Lenacapavir can elevate fentanyl levels, increasing the risk of serious adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring of therapeutic effects and adverse reactions is essential. 3. Flunisolide (inhaled): Lenacapavir may increase flunisolide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Flurazepam: Lenacapavir may enhance the effects of flurazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Flutamide: Lenacapavir may increase flutamide levels, necessitating careful monitoring for adverse effects. 6. Fluticasone Furoate: Lenacapavir may significantly increase fluticasone levels, potentially leading to systemic corticosteroid effects such as Cushing syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor. 7. Fosamprenavir: Lenacapavir may elevate fosamprenavir levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 8. Fosaprepitant: Lenacapavir may increase fosaprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Fostamatinib: Lenacapavir may increase fostamatinib levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Fostemsavir: Lenacapavir may elevate fostemsavir levels. Use caution and monitor. 11. Futibatinib: Lenacapavir may increase futibatinib levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 12. Ganaxolone: Lenacapavir may increase ganaxolone levels. Use caution and monitor. 13. Gefitinib: Lenacapavir may elevate gefitinib levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Gepirone: Lenacapavir may increase gepirone levels. It is recommended to reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when co-administered with lenacapavir. Monitor closely. 15. Glasdegib: Lenacapavir may increase glasdegib levels. Use caution and monitor. 16. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Lenacapavir may elevate levels of this combination therapy. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 17. Guanfacine: Lenacapavir may increase guanfacine levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Haloperidol: Lenacapavir may elevate haloperidol levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Hydrocodone: Lenacapavir may increase hydrocodone levels, necessitating close monitoring for adverse effects, including respiratory depression. 20. Hydrocortisone: Lenacapavir may significantly increase hydrocortisone levels, raising the risk of toxicities such as Cushing syndrome or adrenal suppression. Initiate dexamethasone at the lowest dose, monitor, and titrate accordingly. 21. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Lenacapavir may increase hydroxyprogesterone levels. Use caution and monitor. 22. Ibrutinib: Lenacapavir may elevate ibrutinib levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 23. Idelalisib: Lenacapavir may increase idelalisib levels. Use caution and monitor. 24. Ifosfamide: Lenacapavir may elevate ifosfamide levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Imatinib: Lenacapavir may increase imatinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 26. Indinavir: Lenacapavir may elevate indinavir levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 27. Irinotecan (all formulations): Lenacapavir may increase irinotecan levels, necessitating close monitoring for adverse effects. 28. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Lenacapavir may elevate isavuconazonium levels. Use caution and monitor. 29. Isosorbide Dinitrate and Mononitrate: Lenacapavir may increase levels of these drugs. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 30. Istradefylline: Lenacapavir may elevate istradefylline levels. Use caution and monitor. 31. Itraconazole: Lenacapavir may increase itraconazole levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 32. Ivabradine: Lenacapavir may elevate ivabradine levels. Use caution and monitor. 33. Ivacaftor: Lenacapavir may increase ivacaftor levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 34. Ivosidenib: Lenacapavir may elevate ivosidenib levels. Use caution and monitor. 35. Ixabepilone: Lenacapavir may increase ixabepilone levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 36. Ixazomib: Lenacapavir may elevate ixazomib levels. Use caution and monitor. 37. Ketamine: Lenacapavir may increase ketamine levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. 38. Lacosamide: Lenacapavir may elevate lacosamide levels. Use caution and monitor. 39. Lansoprazole: Lenacapavir may increase lansoprazole levels. Therapeutic monitoring is recommended. In all cases, lenacapavir's inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism may persist for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, necessitating prolonged monitoring of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates. Adjustments to therapy and close monitoring of therapeutic effects and adverse reactions are strongly recommended.
